newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB wheat pool prices up A$2.00-plus a tonne.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB wheat pool prices up A$2.00-plus a tonne.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) increased estimated 1996/97 pool returns further with benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW) rising by A$2.00 a tonne, the AWB said in a statement.

Price increases ranged up to A$9.00 a tonne for noodle wheat in Western Australia, A$7.00 a tonne for noodle wheat in eastern Australia and by A$7.00 a tonne for Australian Prime Hard (APH), the AWB said.
"A firmer market and the benefits of capturing higher prices through a longer sales period prompted the AWB's decision to increase prices," Ron Storey, AWB general manager merchandising, said.
Particular increases had occurred in the prime hard and noodle wheat pools, he said.
All other pool prices increased by A$2.00 a tonne with the exception of feed wheat which rose by A$5.00 a tonne.
This reflected a firm market and high international corn prices, Storey said.
The durum pool, already closed, has an unchanged price.
The next pools update will be issued on Tuesday, April 1.
